## 2026-10-08 Twelve Data daily-credit meter boundary recheck

- Rechecked Twelve Data's current first-party usage-control and credit docs.
  The Basic plan's distinct pools are 8 credits per fixed minute and 800 credits
  per UTC calendar day; the daily pool resets at 00:00 UTC. The documented
  `/api_usage` endpoint costs one API credit and reports current plan/remaining
  credits, while response headers report credits used/left. The first-party
  material reviewed does not define a separate daily-credit counter in the
  endpoint response or say that daily credit usage can be inferred from its
  request-count fields.
- Therefore the existing adapter behavior is intentionally conservative: it
  records the header pool as `credits_per_minute`, preserves documented
  `current_usage`/`daily_usage` request counters separately, and never maps
  those request counts into weighted daily credits. `/api_usage` cannot be
  safely admitted while `credits_per_day` usage is unknown, because the usage
  probe itself consumes one credit. No API-key request was made.
- Focused regression tests passed `15/15` across Twelve Data parsing,
  account-usage observation, and quota-contract admission. This confirms the
  code does not silently substitute requests for credits; it does not clear
  the provider's daily-credit admission blocker.
- Sources: [Twelve Data usage control](https://support.twelvedata.com/en/articles/5713553-control-over-api-usage)
  and [credit pools/reset behavior](https://support.twelvedata.com/en/articles/5615854-credits).

  `api_key_*` monthly counters/limits. The provider quota contract is scoped
  to the API key, but the adapter previously seeded it from account-wide
  `current_total_monthly_calls` and `monthly_call_credit`. It now requires

## 2026-10-04 FINRA async usage-contract and partial-byte audit

- Rechecked FINRA's first-party Query API documentation and FAQ. FINRA states
  that sync calls return at most 5,000 records/3 MB, async calls at most
  100,000 records without that 3 MB body ceiling, and async request throttling
  is 20 per minute per dataset/API account. The status URL should be polled no
  more often than once per minute; completed presigned results expire two
  hours after completion or 24 hours after creation, whichever comes first.
- FINRA's FAQ confirms Public credentials have a 10 GB download allocation
  per month and are made inactive until the first day of the next month if it
  is exceeded. Exact reset timezone and byte convention remain unpublished;
  the provider-defined reset plus conservative rolling 31-day safety envelope
  and baseline requirement therefore remain appropriate. The async response
  has no per-response payload-size ceiling, so this does not provide a safe
  per-job maximum.
- Fixed a quota-measurement defect in `FINRAProvider.download_async_result`:
  bytes yielded before a stream exception or configured-bound failure are now
  included in transport telemetry instead of appearing as zero. The
  end-to-end runtime test then exposed that policy quota windows released
  request/byte units on failed calls even when a provider response had arrived.
  Failure settlement now consumes the measured non-concurrency dimensions
  whenever a response was observed, matching the durable coordinator; it still
  releases concurrency leases. Regression coverage verifies both the partial
  transport measurement and the provider-policy monthly-byte debit.
- The focused FINRA adapter, direct-transport, provider-runtime, and
  quota-contract suites passed **211/211** after the fix; Ruff lint/format
  checks and `git diff --check` passed. No provider HTTP requests were made.
- The async adapter itself remains intentionally non-routable at the default
  zero-byte bound. Successful bodies are currently accumulated in memory and
  there is no durable streaming/pagination/recovery job. A complete solution
  still needs a quota-aware persistent result pipeline; do not treat this
  narrow accounting fix as async integration acceptance. First-party sources:
  `https://developer.finra.org/node/1146`,
  `https://developer.finra.org/docs`,
  `https://developer.finra.org/support`.

## 2026-10-04 FINRA Daily List cursor integrity

- FINRA OTC Daily List ingestion now has a page adapter for the existing durable
  market-event cursor service. It validates authoritative paging headers,
  retains every well-formed returned row (including dates outside the query
  filter), emits rows from a page even when the reported total changes, and
  restarts that segment from offset zero. Stable Daily List IDs make replay
  idempotent; rows without IDs use a full-payload digest plus deterministic
  page/occurrence identity, so even identical provider rows in one page do not
  collapse. Explicitly bounded date windows split when the 500,000 offset
  ceiling would prevent a complete read; unbounded/unsplittable windows fail
  retryably instead of claiming completion or dropping data.
- FINRA's current Query API documentation describes 5,000 synchronous rows,
  a 3 MB response ceiling, 500,000 maximum offset, and response headers for
  totals/offset/page limits. The current ORF file contract is documented in the
  existing provider review; it is separate from the FINRA Gateway API key and
  remains unapproved for complete OTC routing. The adapter change does not
  establish OTC source rights or complete-universe acceptance.
- Added regressions for multi-page cursor continuation, missing totals,
  offset-driven date splitting, unstable-total restart with current-page row
  retention, out-of-window row retention, and collision-safe fallback event
  identity. FINRA/provider event/quota unit selection passed `153/153`; changed

## 2026-09-25 FMP reset-source conflict

- The current official FMP API FAQ states that the Basic 250-call allowance
  resets every 24 hours at 15:00 `America/New_York` ([FAQ](https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/de/faqs?code=statements)), but newer official FMP

  to invent a reset. The deterministic `15:00 America/New_York` contract is
  retained for existing fixtures, while admission remains dependent on
  reviewed account evidence before FMP is considered fully verified. The
  trailing-30-day bandwidth pool and complete operation-byte map remain
  required.

## 2026-09-17 lossless, resumable provider-event ingestion

- Replaced the Alpaca corporate-action page bound with a durable cursor
  workflow. `InstrumentEventPageSnapshot` retains each raw provider envelope;
  `InstrumentEventFetchState` retains the provider, query fingerprint, page
  number, continuation token, cumulative normalized counts, and completion
  state.
- Event refreshes process one page per provider call, pin incomplete work to
  the provider that issued the cursor, and resume from that cursor on the next
  job. A fresh cache from another provider cannot strand an incomplete page
  chain. Repeated persisted cursors fail closed rather than looping.
- Alpaca requests all documented corporate-action families. Families not yet
  represented by the normalized event enum remain in the immutable raw page
  snapshot. The direct Alpaca compatibility method follows every page.

  Alembic head after merging the existing `b0c1d2e3f4a5` and

- Marketstack EOD history now follows the provider's returned pagination metadata rather than treating a response as a single page; progress guards prevent cursor loops, and explicit/latest/bulk paths reserve a conservative calendar-day page count against the monthly request budget.

- Robinhood tokenized quote accounting now reserves four requests for the asset lookup plus the provider-specific three-attempt 429 retry ceiling; successful two-request reads settle observed usage without permitting an unsafe under-reserved retry path.
- FINRA authenticated short-interest and Daily List calls now reserve two
  requests: the cold OAuth token exchange plus the dataset POST. Warm token
  caches may consume one upstream call, but the runtime remains conservative
  and never undercounts a cold process.

  cold ticker-directory lookup plus submissions read. The keyless live profile

## 2026-09-16 SEC/Nasdaq/Finnhub hardening and authoritative gate

- SEC future-listing materialization now requires corroborated, resolved
  multi-provider evidence with exact symbol/company agreement and either a
  shared venue MIC or a shared FIGI/ISIN/CUSIP from at least two sources.
  Single-source, incomplete, conflicting, and unresolved-venue candidates are
  quarantined; later ambiguous evidence can quarantine legacy provisional
  records rather than silently activating them.
- Nasdaq NMS/equity and ETF reconciliation now fails closed on declared-total
  or cursor gaps, wrong quote types, duplicate listing keys, unknown venues,
  and unmappable MICs. Successful reconciliation records deterministic
  expected/observed/missing MIC coverage and per-MIC counts. FINRA OTC remains
  explicitly outside the authoritative Nasdaq absence scope pending its own
  complete source reconciliation.
- Finnhub routing now models both reviewed dimensions: 60 calls/minute and a
  hard 30 calls/second ceiling. Every reviewed operation reserves both
  dimensions, while existing operator overrides remain preserved when config
  promotion refreshes the provider row.
- Validation after these changes: full backend unit suite `2,273/2,273`;
  focused SEC/universe and provider/quota/runtime contracts `313/313`;
  authoritative Docker-backed backend gate `2,659/2,659`, `81.90%` combined
  coverage, 89 warnings, isolated testcontainer session
  `22b7481d-c4a1-4d15-ae69-7900026793f8`; Ruff passed. No provider calls or
  credentials were used by these checks.
- This does not close the branch. The exact current-SHA live matrix is still
  unaccepted while the worktree is dirty and provider-native baselines,
  byte/account/source/legal controls, complete OTC reconciliation, target
  secret-store verification, deferred-provider decisions, and the final shadow
  gate remain owner-controlled. Do not integrate, deploy, activate routing,
  or begin the 30-day shadow run from this checkpoint.

## 2026-10-06 FINRA history continuation hardening

- Closed a no-loss defect in FINRA OTC Daily List history reads. For unbounded
  or one-sided date ranges, the adapter now requests FINRA's authoritative
  available-partitions index, validates that `calendarDay` is its sole
  partition field, and carries every returned date in a durable cursor. It
  then queries each date as an exact partition instead of issuing one global
  query that can strand results past FINRA's 500,000-offset ceiling. It does
  not guess a start date or impose a local date/page cap. The raw partition
  response is included in provider telemetry/persistence.
- If a single Daily List day itself exceeds synchronous pagination, and for
  analogous FINRA short-interest offset blockers, returned rows and the
  unresolved continuation cursor are now preserved. A blocked cursor is not
  silently cleared: ordinary refreshes avoid futile repeats; the admin refresh
  endpoints accept `retry_blocked=true` after an alternate retrieval path is
  available. Updated `docs/data-providers.md` to distinguish this exceptional
  unresolved case from the now-partitioned full historical scan.
- No external FINRA request was made. Focused provider/service coverage passes
  `57/57`; the admin route regression passes `1/1` with a scoped Docker
  testcontainer. Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` pass. The broader
  provider/live acceptance, one-day-overflow alternative retrieval, ORF
  entitlement, universe, secret-store, and shadow gates remain open.

  credential is free for individuals and capped at 10 GB/month; FINRA says
  usage can be monitored in the API Console and disables an exhausted Public
  credential until the first day of the following month. FINRA publishes 1,200
  synchronous requests/minute/IP and 20 async submissions/minute/dataset/account.

  official docs do not publish a numeric Sandbox request ceiling, reset
  boundary, or per-operation quota schedule. Free Sandbox removes the API
  access fee concern; it does not establish the request allowance or reset.

  HTTP 500 twice (three transport attempts total), while operation accounting
  reserved only the logical request count. Centralized the retry bound and
  changed Dinari's minimum operation costs to worst-case HTTP attempts (single
  request = 3; two requests = 6; symbol corporate actions = 9). The explicit
  `DINARI_SANDBOX_QUOTA_PROFILE` validator now rejects any cost below that
  implementation-derived minimum. No arbitrary provider limit was added; the
  account quota profile is still required and undocumented dimensions stay
  blocking.

  request billing is per ticker in a query and points operators to the account
  dashboard for current usage. The official FAQ/contact pages conflict on the
  Free allowance (100 versus 1,000 requests/month); the existing contract
  conservatively retains 100. Neither reviewed page resolves the number of
  quota units charged for an exchange ticker-directory page, so discovery
  remains disabled until that cost is evidenced. No usage dashboard was
  queried and no Marketstack requests were made.

  quota-contract unit suites passed **256/256**; Ruff check/format and

## 2026-10-11 Finnhub directory request reduction

  the adapter had been turning that one response into synthetic 500-row pages.
  Since the reconciler requested each page separately, it re-downloaded and
  re-archived the entire provider response for every 500 symbols. The adapter
  now returns all filtered rows from the single response, with offset slicing
  only for callers that explicitly resume at a nonzero offset. This preserves
  every returned symbol while reducing a normal universe run to one Finnhub

privileged account or alter target policies as part of this preparation. Also
verify the resolved chain/status after any separately authorized deployment
configuration, rather than inferring it from seed order.

Search results are cached; new canonical identity/profile resolution requires
